independentMathEvidence.averagePowerDerivation: With theta=omega*t, cos(theta)*cos(theta+phi)=[cos(phi)+cos(2*theta+phi)]/2. Integral of cos(2*omega*t+phi) over T=2*pi/omega is [sin(2*omega*T+phi)-sin(phi)]/(2*omega)=0. Hence P=Um*Im*cos(phi)/2=U*I*cos(phi).
independentMathEvidence.rmsDerivation: Mean cos(theta)^2 over T is 1/2, so U=Um/sqrt(2) and I=Im/sqrt(2). The amplitude product alone is neither instantaneous p nor mean P.
independentMathEvidence.phaseAndReactiveSigns: Phi=current phase minus voltage phase. For ideal L, i=Im*sin(theta), phi=-pi/2; for ideal C, i=Im*cos(theta+pi/2), phi=+pi/2. Under conventional absorbed reactive-power sign, Q=-UI*sin(phi), so L has positive Q and C negative Q. This sign check is reviewer mathematics; the draft does not introduce a contradictory Q formula.
independentMathEvidence.positivePower: At fixed positive RMS U/I, phi=0 gives P=UI. For a passive consuming range 0<abs(phi)<pi/2, P is positive but below UI; negative instantaneous intervals do not imply negative mean power. A pure resistor has p=Um*Im*cos(theta)^2>=0.
independentMathEvidence.zeroPower: For ideal pure L/C, phi=+/-pi/2 gives P=0 despite current and alternating instantaneous energy transfer. Real resistance/losses invalidate the zero-loss conclusion.
independentMathEvidence.negativeMeanPowerLimit: If cos(phi)<0, the signed receipt formula implies a section supplies net energy. The drafts do not claim a consuming ideal RLC load operates in this range. This is distinct from the historical positive threshold cos(phi)<0.85.
independentMathEvidence.inductorQuarterCycleEnergy: For Figure 47's ideal L, p=(Um*Im/2)*sin(2*theta). Integral from theta=0 to pi/2 is Um*Im/(2*omega)=L*Im^2/2; the next quarter has the opposite integral. Thus one complete voltage cycle has equal received/returned energy and zero average.
independentMathEvidence.figureNormalizedProduct: Let a=u/Um=cos(theta), b=i/Im=sin(theta), and c=p/(Um*Im/2)=sin(2*theta). Then c=2*a*b, not a*b. The candidate's separate plotted ordinate amplitudes 62,44,100 are illustrative and not physical units or raw ordinate multiplication.
independentMathEvidence.figureZeros: For t/T=0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1,1.25,1.5,1.75, p is zero at alternating i/u zeros. In the 640px candidate these correspond to x=48,92.5,137,181.5,226,270.5,315,359.5 on y=180.
independentMathEvidence.limitations: Independent equations and visual source sign/zero observations agree with the existing native geometry receipt. Mathematical expectations do not establish exact source alphabets, tiny arrows, dash intent, numerical amplitudes, or exact scan endpoint times.
